newsitem.title: UK: LME pre-market sleeps, but zinc nearing $1,400.
newsitem.headline: LME pre-market sleeps, but zinc nearing $1,400.

text.p: Business ticked over during Friday LME pre-market trading, with most base metals languishing in unexciting bands, although zinc was creeping higher, traders noted.
"There is nothing really happening here - it is all a bit lacklustre," one said.
Zinc was gearing up for a test of $1,400 - an obvious psychological and technical objective - having started an upside attack on Thursday.
Fundamentals are broadly supportive, with the market nicely balanced at present, although these would change if talk of Chinese deliveries into Singapore becomes fact, they said.
Three months prices were around 4-3/4 year highs of $1,396 a tonne, a $3 gain from Thursday's kerb.
Elsewhere in the complex, copper was basically marching on the spot, with an 1,800-tonne stock fall of moderate interest. Trade at $2,588 was just $2.50 up from yesterday.
The backwardation was around $120, basis cash/threes, but the forward market may be reluctant to challenge $2,600 after repeated rebuffs at that level.
Aluminium held in a tight $1,579-1,584 band, paying little heed to yet another 2,650-tonne inventory fall. Business was at $1,580, down $4.
Later this morning the market will focus on May IPAI production data, with a smal drop in output being forecast in some quarters.
Nickel prices edged up from early lows back up to unchanged levels of $7,160, helped in part by a modest 90-tonne stock fall.

Traders were also cautious over developments at the strike-bound Inco Sudbury facilities, where talks are resuming. The union said late on Thursday there may not be fresh developments until after the July maintainance shutdown.
Tin was quietly steadier at $5,640, a gain of $25, while lead was quoted at a slightly steadier $626/628. Alloy was also steady at $1,470/80 a tonne.
